data.title: Conditional Probability in Two-Way Tables
data.description: Practice calculating conditional probabilities by analyzing contingency tables and determining marginal totals from given frequencies.

challenges.question: Given a member is Male, what is the probability they are Reading? Enter P(Reading | Male) as a decimal (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Only look at the "Male" row. The cell Reading in that row is 14. The row total is 40. Divide: 14 ÷ 40.

challenges.question: Given a member is Cafeteria, what is the probability they are Grade 7? Enter P(Grade 7 | Cafeteria) as a decimal (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Only look at the "Cafeteria" column. The cell Grade 7 in that column is 28. The column total is 64. Divide: 28 ÷ 64.

challenges.question: Given a member is Under 30, what is the probability they are Brand B? Enter P(Brand B | Under 30) as a decimal (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Only look at the "Under 30" row. The cell Brand B in that row is 18. The row total is 60. Divide: 18 ÷ 60.

challenges.question: Given a member is Eats, what is the probability they are Weekend? Enter P(Weekend | Eats) as a decimal (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Only look at the "Eats" column. The cell Weekend in that column is 50. The column total is 95. Divide: 50 ÷ 95.

data.educationalContext: Conditional probability allows us to find the likelihood of an event occurring given that another specific condition has already been met, which is essential for analyzing statistical dependence in real-world data.
